text: Euler double rarefaction: positivity at every stage A one-dimensional MUSCL finite-volume Euler double rarefaction combines Lax–Friedrichs fluxes, SSPRK(3,3) and mean-preserving positive-state scaling at each stage. Check the admissible CFL, density/pressure in cell means and face states, and conservation budgets from actual shared boundary fluxes separately. These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems. Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved. Download and execute the supplement Run inside atlas-euler-positivity-2026-11-23-r2 from the ZIP. This command executes all 1 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs. python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python -m pytest -q python run.py --input inputs.json --output output Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it. Euler double rarefaction: positivity at every stage Evolve the existing strong double rarefaction on 128/256/512 cells, connecting mean-preserving positivity scaling to MUSCL, global LF fluxes and SSPRK(3,3). Log density, pressure and boundary budgets for every FE substep and SSP convex combination. Methods, equations, figures and references Assumptions, units and boundaries Fix gamma1.4, x in [0,1], discontinuity x0=.5, outer primitive states(1,-2,.4)/(1,2,.4) and T=.15. The low-density central state remains strictly positive; this is not a vacuum-generating case. Use fixed global LF splitting speed a4 and dt*a/dx<=.4; assert every actual endpoint satisfies |u|+c<=a and the sufficient dt*a/dx<=1/2 condition. Editorial clarification The same fixed physical input as the existing double rarefaction uses gamma=1.4, left/right (rho,u,p)=(1,-2,.4)/(1,2,.4), [0,1], x0=.5 and t=.15. Its middle state has small positive density/pressure, unlike separate vacuum-generating data. Stage scaling is connected to sufficient CFL and Lax–Friedrichs wave-speed conditions for this scoped example, without certifying existing WENO, DG, MHD or general equations of state. Adopted numerical method Unlimited conservative central linear reconstruction is scaled toward its mean with one common theta per cell until both endpoint densities/pressures are positive. The two endpoint mean remains the original conserved mean. Shared LF FE updates are combined by SSPRK(3,3), reconstructing/limiting before every flux stage. Epsilon1e-13 is a reconstruction target, not an injected density/energy floor. Retain negative raw endpoint pressures, then separately measure limited endpoints, FE means, SSP convex means, theta and all three boundary-flux conservation budgets. Cross-check the closed symmetric fan against the prior independent logarithmic-pressure root evaluator; record errors/refinement against conserved Gauss8/16 cell means. Verification limits and failures Evidence covers this one P1 FV update and fixed input, not general MUSCL/WENO/DG, characteristic reconstruction, reflecting walls, vacuum generation or multidimensional positivity. Unlimited central slopes have no TVD, maximum-principle or nonoscillation guarantee. Raw pressure is evaluated only where raw density is positive; nonpositive raw density has its own count. Reference pressure is p(mean conserved q), not mean pressure. Gallery plots are saved one-dimensional x-t fields, not two-dimensional flow. No ExactPack or separate PDE engine is executed. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed. Xiangxiong Zhang and Chi-Wang Shu (2010). On positivity-preserving high order discontinuous Galerkin schemes for compressible Euler equations on rectangular meshes · DOI: 10.1016/j.jcp.2010.08.016 Review scope / review_level: author manuscript selected sections actually inspected: §2 Theorem2.1, Remarks2.2/2.4/2.6/2.7; §4.3 distinguishes vacuum input Inspected positivity conditions, LF proof, stage limiting and speed-bound caution. This applies the framework to P1 FV; it does not reproduce the paper’s vacuum test or third-order DG scheme. David I. Ketcheson, Randall J. LeVeque and Mauricio J. del Razo (2020). Riemann Problems and Jupyter Solutions: The Euler equations of gas dynamics · DOI: 10.1137/1.9781611976212 Review scope / review_level: official chapter sections Riemann invariants, exact solution, symmetric expansion and vacuum; official exact_solvers/euler.py integral_curve_1/3 inspected read-only Read the official invariants, symmetric expansion and vacuum conditions. The fixed values inherit the existing atlas case and differ from this chapter’s example. No Clawpack software is executed or copied. Chi-Wang Shu and Stanley Osher (1988).
